office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the state budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Lillian Ortiz-Self, House Majority Caucus Chair and a school counselor, faces Libertarian Bruce Guthrie, a retired executive and teacher. Ortiz-Self voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million; repealing that tax is Guthrie's top issue.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative and House Majority Caucus Chair, an Everett School District counselor, campaigning on education, behavioral health, child care, immigrant protections and reproductive rights.
highlights: House Majority Caucus Chair; sits on Education and Children, Youth and Families [S1]
Voted for ESSB 6346 and ESSB 5813's capital gains and estate tax changes [S5][S7]
Says she introduced bills on private detention oversight and notice of federal employment-document requests [S2]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list [S6]

taxes.basis: Recorded votes for ESSB 6346 (tax on income over $1 million) and ESSB 5813 (more progressive capital gains and estate taxes).

spending.basis: Says the state needs leadership 'ready and willing to invest in Washington' to backfill federal cuts to services.

housing.basis: Co-sponsored and voted for EHB 1217 rent and fee limits and voted for ESHB 2266 supportive-housing siting.

safety.basis: Pairs expanding behavioral health care and gun violence prevention with 'strengthening and diversifying law enforcement.'

climate.basis: Cites climate action and clean-economy infrastructure and voted for the 2025 clean fuels bill; no carbon-pricing statement.

experience.basis: Long-serving representative and eight-year House Majority Caucus Chair.

local-control.basis: Voted for ESHB 2266, which sets state rules requiring cities to allow supportive housing and shelters.

immigration.basis: Says states must be 'the first line of defense' and that she introduced detention-oversight and ICE-notice bills to protect immigrants.

social.basis: Campaign site states abortion protection is something she has 'long fought for' and must keep fighting for.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which amended and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Libertarian candidate in his seventh campaign, a retired sales and marketing executive and teacher from Edmonds, whose top issue is repealing the state income tax.
highlights: Top issue: 'Oppose/Repeal State Income Tax'; also cut gas taxes and state spending [S1][S2]
Would arrest shoplifters and bike thieves and stop 'subsidizing' homelessness [S2]
Supports barring 'genetic males' from girls' sports in grades 9 and up, school vouchers and legislative term limits [S2]

taxes.basis: Repeatedly calls for repealing the state income tax and cutting gas and other state taxes.

spending.basis: Pamphlet and site both call for cutting record-level state spending.

housing.basis: Blames high rents on property taxes and land over-regulation that limits supply.

safety.basis: Proposes reducing homelessness by arresting shoplifters and bike thieves and ending subsidies.

climate.basis: Opposes the gas tax and says the Climate Commitment Act and cap-and-invest have raised gas prices without helping the environment.

immigration.basis: Would help ICE deport people convicted of crimes but not cooperate in deporting others: a mixed position.

reform.basis: Supports term limits of four terms for legislators.

social.basis: Supports barring 'genetic males' from competing against girls in grades 9 and above.

experience.basis: Has never held elected office; seventh Libertarian campaign.
